VERSION.value: netlib odepack (double precision: opkdmain.f, opkda1.f, opkda2.f), as fetched 2026-09-12

value.lineage: Netlib Fortran ODE solvers descended from GEAR (1974): variable-step variable-order Adams (non-stiff) and BDF (stiff) methods with error control, a corrector iteration and a Jacobian strategy chosen by the method flag MF. Sibling of QUADPACK/EISPACK in the vault; ancestor of scipy.integrate.odeint (which wraps LSODA).

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: stiff and non-stiff initial value problems

value.built_to: integrate ODE systems with automatic step and order selection, including stiff systems whose fast modes would otherwise force absurdly small steps
value.pressure: stiffness: time scales separated by 10^10 in Robertson's problem; error tolerances; work limits
value.success_means: the requested tolerance is met in a bounded number of steps; a method mismatched to the problem is reported, not silently wrong

value.pressure: stiffness (widely separated time scales), accuracy tolerance, step budget
value.failure_condition: the non-stiff method's stability region forces steps ~1/|lambda|: the integrator exhausts its step budget (ISTATE=-1) or diverges

cut.note: the famous names (LSODE, Gear's method, BDF) sit above a small set of mechanisms that are each replaceable: a scaled-derivative history array, a predictor that is pure addition, a corrector with a self-measured convergence rate, a weighted-RMS error test, a three-candidate step/order chooser with hysteresis and hold-off, a Jacobian refresh policy keyed to how far the iteration matrix has drifted, and a failure ladder with escalating retreats

provenance.grade_basis: Techne FOSSIL_PACKET.json PROVENANCE_GRADE where issued, else the record's handoff string mapped (populated per R34; Harmonia may re-grade)

organs.mechanism: state is kept as YH(i,j+1) = h^j y_i^(j) / j! for j = 0..NQ, i.e. the solution and its scaled Taylor coefficients at the current point, one column per order; a change of step size h -> rh*h is a column-wise rescale by rh^j (DSTODE 175-180); a change of order adds or drops a column; the array is also what the interpolant reads
organs.input: the accepted correction ACOR and the coefficients EL(j) after a successful step
organs.output: the current state for every consumer (predictor, error test, order change, interpolation, restart)
organs.update: per accepted step (470: YH(i,j) += EL(j)*ACOR(i)); rescaled on every h change
assumptions: the scaled derivatives are meaningful, i.e. the solution is smooth enough at the current order; the failure ladder (KFLAG <= -3) says explicitly when it stops trusting them
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: one representation serves prediction, correction, error control, order change, step change and dense output; nothing is recomputed from past solution values
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: after repeated error-test failures the accumulated derivatives are assumed wrong and the array is truncated to order 1 with a fresh f evaluation (640-650); no measurement
organs.human_prior: Nordsieck (1962) representation chosen over storing past y values (the multistep textbook form); the choice is what makes step changes cheap
organs.source_boundary: every YH read/write in DSTODE; the LYH slice of RWORK in the driver

organs.mechanism: advance the history array to TN+H by NQ passes of in-place column additions YH1(I) += YH1(I+NYH) from the highest order down: multiplication by the Pascal-triangle matrix with no multiplications; the same loop with subtraction (440-445, 510-515) is the exact retraction used on failure
organs.output: predicted YH at TN+H (first column = predicted y)
assumptions: the Taylor form of YH (the organ above); exactness of the retraction relies on the additions being reversible in floating point only approximately (not measured)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the predictor costs ~N*NQ additions and no function evaluations

organs.mechanism: up to MAXCOR=3 iterations of either functional iteration (MITER=0: y <- y0 + el(1)*(h f(y) - yh2)) or the chord method (solve P dy = h f - (yh2 + acor) with P = I - h*el0*J held fixed); after each iteration the weighted norm DEL of the correction is taken and CRATE = max(0.2*CRATE, DEL/DELP) estimates the contraction rate; the stopping test is DEL*min(1, 1.5*CRATE) <= TESCO(2,NQ)*CONIT, i.e. the iteration is declared converged when its PREDICTED remaining error is below the local error test scale, not when the last correction is tiny; divergence (DEL > 2*DELP at M >= 2) aborts early
organs.input: predicted YH, the iteration matrix P (if chord), f
organs.output: the accumulated correction ACOR and the corrected y, or a convergence failure
organs.state: CRATE (persists across steps, reset to 0.7 when P is refreshed), DELP
assumptions: contraction is roughly geometric so one ratio predicts the tail
for the chord method P may be stale (it is deliberately reused; see the refresh policy organ)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the convergence test is calibrated to the error test, so no iterations are spent beyond what the step can use; CRATE lets a slow iteration stop early and trigger a matrix refresh instead of burning MAXCOR
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: with MITER=0 on a stiff problem the iteration diverges for any step larger than ~1/|lambda| and the ladder shrinks h until the budget is exhausted (the record's failure)
organs.human_prior: MAXCOR=3 and the 0.2/1.5 constants are Hindmarsh's tuning; not derived

organs.mechanism: error weights EWT(i) = RTOL*|y_i| + ATOL(i) are recomputed from the current y before every step (driver 250-260) and inverted; every norm in the integrator is the RMS of v_i/EWT_i (DVNORM); the local error estimate is the norm of the accumulated correction divided by TESCO(2,NQ) (a method constant), and the step is accepted iff that is <= 1
organs.output: EWT vector; the scalar DSM; accept/reject
assumptions: a mixed relative/absolute tolerance is the right notion of close; components with EWT <= 0 are an illegal input (driver 510, ISTATE=-6)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: one scalar drives every decision (convergence, acceptance, step and order choice), and it is dimensionless so the same constants serve every problem
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: TOLSF = uround * ||y||_EWT > 1 means the tolerance is below machine precision; the driver returns ISTATE=-2 (520) rather than loop

organs.mechanism: after a step (success or failure) three step-size multipliers are computed from error estimates at orders NQ-1, NQ, NQ+1: RH = 1/(c * D^(1/(q+1)) + tiny) with c = 1.3, 1.2, 1.4; the largest wins; a change is made only if RH >= 1.1 (else IALTH=3: do not look again for 3 steps); after any change IALTH = NQ+1 steps of hold-off; RMAX caps the increase at 10 (1e4 on the first step, 2 after a failure); on failure RHUP=0 (never raise order) and after two failures RH <= 0.2; the order-up estimate needs the previous step's correction, which is saved into the spare column only when IALTH=1
organs.input: DSM, ACOR, YH(:,L), the saved previous correction, KFLAG
organs.output: new H, new NQ (NQ-1, NQ, NQ+1)
organs.state: IALTH (hold-off counter), RMAX, the spare YH column
assumptions: the local error scales as h^(q+1) (the exponent in each ratio)
changing h or q costs a rescale and destabilises the estimates, hence the hold-off
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the step and order track the solution's smoothness without a fixed schedule; the hysteresis (1.1) and hold-off (IALTH) stop the controller chattering
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the constants 1.3/1.2/1.4 bias toward keeping or lowering order; an order increase is only ever tried from a clean step (RHUP=0 on failure)
organs.human_prior: the safety factors and the 1.1 threshold are tuning; the asymmetric bias against order increase is a design choice recorded in the code, not in the prologue

evidence.ref: vault:odepack-netlib/upstream/opkda1.f:520-630 and 100-125 (same formula on a MAXORD change)

organs.mechanism: the iteration matrix P = I - h*el0*J is NOT rebuilt every step: RC tracks the ratio of the current h*el0 to the one P was built with; P is rebuilt when |RC-1| > CCMAX=0.3, or every MSBP=20 steps, or when the corrector fails to converge with a stale P (JCUR=0 -> refresh and retry the same step before reducing h); refreshing resets CRATE to 0.7
organs.state: RC, NSLP (step of last build), JCUR
organs.update: per step and per convergence failure
assumptions: J changes slowly along the solution; a wrong P only slows the chord iteration, it does not change the fixed point
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the expensive operation (N function evaluations or a user Jacobian plus an LU) is amortised over ~20 steps; a convergence failure is first blamed on staleness, then on the step
organs.human_prior: CCMAX=0.3, MSBP=20 are tuning constants set in the driver (opkdmain.f 110-118)
organs.source_boundary: the IPUP/RC/NSLP/JCUR variables and their tests

organs.mechanism: five ways to build and apply P = I - h*el0*J behind one interface: 1 user dense Jacobian; 2 finite-difference dense (N extra f calls, increment R = max(sqrt(uround)*|y_j|, r0/EWT_j) with r0 = 1000*|h|*uround*N*||f||); 3 a DIAGONAL approximation from ONE extra f call along the predicted correction direction (a diagonal Jacobian-vector estimate; the solve is a vector divide, rescaled when h*el0 changes without a rebuild, DSOLSY 300-390); 4 user banded; 5 finite-difference banded (MBAND extra f calls, columns grouped by band); dense/banded go through LINPACK LU (DGEFA/DGBFA) and back-solve
organs.output: P factored in WM, or IERPJ
organs.state: WM (the factored matrix; for MITER=3 the diagonal and the h*el0 it was built at)
assumptions: for MITER=3 the diagonal approximation is only good when J is nearly diagonal in the EWT scaling; the code cannot tell and the corrector rate (CRATE) is the only signal
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: cost/accuracy of the Newton matrix is a user choice orthogonal to the integrator (DSTODE is independent of MITER, prologue)

organs.mechanism: convergence failure: refresh P if stale, else retract, RMAX=2, h*0.25, count NCF; at MXNCF=10 or h=HMIN -> KFLAG=-2. error-test failure: retract, KFLAG-1, choose h at order NQ or NQ-1 with RHUP=0; after 2 failures h <= 0.2*h; after 3 the history is distrusted: order -> 1, f re-evaluated, h*0.1, IALTH=5; at 10 failures or h=HMIN -> KFLAG=-1. driver: MXSTEP (default 500) steps per call -> ISTATE=-1 with the partial solution returned; T+H == T in floating point -> a warning up to MXHNIL=10 times, then silence, integration continues
organs.output: a retry with a smaller h and/or lower order, or a typed failure return with the state as of the last good step
assumptions: the last accepted state is always recoverable (retraction is exact enough); failures are local, so shrinking h is the right first move
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: every failure is typed (-1 budget, -2 precision, -4 error test, -5 corrector, -6 weights) and returns the solution as far as it got with the offending component (IWORK(16)) named; nothing is silently wrong
organs.failure_landscape: the record's own: a non-stiff method on a stiff problem exhausts MXSTEP (ISTATE=-1) rather than diverging; the ladder makes the failure cheap and legible
organs.human_prior: the retreat factors 0.25 / 0.2 / 0.1 and the counts 10 / 10 / 500 are tuning

organs.mechanism: if the user gives no H0: TOL = max(RTOL, ATOL/|y|) clipped to [100*uround, 1e-3]; H0 = 1/sqrt(1/(TOL*W0^2) + TOL*||f||_EWT^2) with W0 = max(|T|,|TOUT|); capped by |TOUT-T| and HMAX; then RMAX=1e4 lets the first accepted step grow fast
assumptions: a first step that is too small is cheap to recover from (RMAX=1e4 on the first step), so the heuristic errs small
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: removes a user parameter; the two terms balance a time-scale bound and a derivative bound

organs.human_name: DCFODE (Adams to order 12, BDF to order 5)
organs.mechanism: the integration coefficients EL(1..q+1) and the three test constants TESCO(1..3,q) for every order are generated at run time from the coefficients of the product polynomial (x+1)(x+2)...(x+q-1) built by an integer-like recurrence; Adams: integrate the polynomial (PINT, XPIN); BDF: normalise by PC(2); the maximum orders (12, 5) are hard limits of the tables
assumptions: BDF above order 5 is unstable (the human record's reason for MXORDS=5); the table size encodes that prior
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: no stored tables; the same code serves two method families
organs.human_prior: the two families and their order caps

organs.mechanism: the k-th derivative at any T in [TN-HU, TN] is read off the history array by a Horner-like sum over the columns with s = (T-TN)/H and falling-factorial coefficients; no extra f calls; T outside the last step is refused (IFLAG)
assumptions: the history polynomial is accurate over the last step only
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: output at user times decoupled from the step sequence (ITASK=1 interpolates rather than stepping to TOUT)

organs.human_name: DSTODA method switch (DLSODA), read in part
organs.mechanism: (DLSODA only) after each converged corrector the contraction rate is turned into a local Lipschitz-constant estimate PDEST = max(PDEST, RATE/|h*el(1)|); every ICOUNT steps the code computes the step the OTHER family could take (a stability-bounded step for Adams, SM1(NQ)/PDH; an error-bounded step for BDF) and switches only if the other family's step is at least RATIO=5 times larger; a switch resets order and rescales YH
organs.update: per step; decision every ICOUNT steps
assumptions: the corrector's contraction rate is a usable proxy for the spectral radius of h*J (a stiffness detector with no eigenvalue computation)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: removes the user's MF choice -- the record's failure mode (wrong family for the problem) is what this organ exists to prevent
organs.failure_landscape: UNKNOWN by run; by reading the RATIO=5 hysteresis prevents flapping but delays the switch

pressures.condition: the world's state evolves under a rule whose fastest mode decays 10^6-10^10 times faster than the slow behaviour of interest; the organism must report the slow behaviour to a stated tolerance within a bounded number of evaluations of the rule
pressures.resource_or_constraint: a step/evaluation budget (the ancestor's MXSTEP=500 per call) and a tolerance; the rule's derivative is available but its Jacobian is expensive
pressures.failure_condition: budget exhausted before the horizon (the ancestor's ISTATE=-1) or a reported answer outside tolerance
pressures.world_punishes: taking steps at the fast time scale; reporting an answer that drifts from the slow solution
pressures.world_rewards: an organism whose step is bounded by the slow behaviour, not by the fast mode's stability limit
pressures.observable_consequence: evaluations used vs tolerance achieved on the same problem across stiffness ratios (the record's Robertson-type entry point)
pressures.vacuity_condition: a problem with one time scale, or a budget so large that the fast scale can be resolved
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: a fixed tiny step with an unlimited budget; reading the analytic slow manifold if the world exposes it; a lookup of the answer
pressures.cheat_control: an organism handed the exact solution must be scored as passing the tolerance at zero evaluations, and a fixed-step explicit organism must be scored as exhausting the budget at stiffness ratio 10^6: if the world cannot separate those two the pressure is not present

pressures.condition: an organism may build a local linear model of the world's rule at a cost of N evaluations, and each step's inner solve is cheap given the model; the model decays in usefulness as the state moves
pressures.resource_or_constraint: evaluation budget; the model's cost is N times a step's cost
pressures.failure_condition: rebuilding every step (budget) or never rebuilding (inner iteration diverges)
pressures.world_rewards: a refresh policy that reads its own convergence behaviour
pressures.observable_consequence: rebuilds per 100 steps vs inner-iteration failures per 100 steps
pressures.vacuity_condition: the model is free, or the rule is linear so the model never drifts
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: a fixed rebuild period tuned to the test problem
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given a free exact model must show zero inner failures and zero rebuild cost; a policy that rebuilds every step must be scored as spending N-fold budget: the world must price the rebuild or the pressure is absent

pressures.condition: an organism chooses its own step/resolution from an error signal it computes; changes are costly (rescaling, invalidated estimates) and the error signal is noisy at the step scale
pressures.resource_or_constraint: each change costs a rescale and a hold-off during which estimates are unreliable
pressures.failure_condition: oscillating resolution (step up, fail, step down, ...) that wastes the budget
pressures.world_punishes: a high change count per accepted step
pressures.world_rewards: hysteresis and hold-off that still track real changes in the solution's smoothness
pressures.observable_consequence: changes per accepted step and rejected steps per accepted step on a problem whose smoothness varies (a known transient)
pressures.vacuity_condition: a constant-smoothness problem where one step size is right throughout
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: never change the step (fails the tracking half); change only downward
pressures.cheat_control: a controller fed the exact optimal step sequence must score zero rejections; a controller with hysteresis disabled must show more changes on the same problem: if the world cannot see the difference it is not measuring chatter
